subject: Context tiling / how long contexts get split on invoices
messages:
From: Rajiv Mehra <rajiv@acmehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Health Billing <billing@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Context tiling / invoice example ask

Marcus —

Thanks for the call this morning. Our finance team is trying to reconcile the August invoice and theres one area they want an explicit example for: when we send really long chat sessions (40k+ token histories) and your runtime splits those into multiple billing windows, how does that get represented line-by-line on the invoice?

They want to see a concrete sample: how many lines, how the token accounting maps to the request id, and whether theres any rounding or minimum applied per tiled chunk. Attached is the August invoice extract we have (sample_invoice_acme_202508.pdf) and a small CSV with one thread token/time series we exported.

Can you provide one or two sample mappings (raw request -> tiled line items -> billed tokens) and call out where rounding/minimums would kick in? Also flag any edge cases we should expect when context lengths move across day boundaries.

Thanks — appreciate a short example we can hand to our GL team.

—Rajiv
Rajiv Mehra
Head of Payments Operations
Acme Health
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Mehra <rajiv@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Sep 2025 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Context tiling / invoice example ask

Rajiv —

Thanks for the note and the attachments; those were helpful. Short answer up front: one long chat can become multiple invoice lines when the request triggers context "tiling" (we call them "tiles" internally) due to either maximum context window per model instance or the billing quantum. Each tile is billed independently, subject to the per-tile minimum and our rounding rules.

I'll attach two short examples below (inline) showing:
- Example A: single 42k-token chat split into 3 tiles because of a 16k token per-tile cap;
- Example B: 18k-token chat that is tiled by the billing quantum (1,000 token minimum per tile) causing an effective rounding bump.

Key points:
- We record request IDs so each tile references the original request; the invoice shows tiled line items with a suffix (e.g., request-1234_tile-1/3).
- Rounding/minimums are applied per billed tile, not at the aggregate request level. That means small tails can incur the minimum.
- If a tile boundary crosses a billing day boundary, the tiles are attributed to the day the tile was processed (timestamped) — so a single logical request can appear across two invoice dates.

Inline examples (simplified):

Example A (42,100 tokens total)
- Request: request-1234 (42,100 tokens)
- Model per-tile cap: 16,000 tokens -> tiles: 16,000 + 16,000 + 10,100
- Per-tile rounding quantum: 100 tokens (billed in 100-token increments) -> billed: 16,000, 16,000, 10,100 -> no rounding change here
- Invoice lines: request-1234_tile-1 (16,000), _tile-2 (16,000), _tile-3 (10,100)

Example B (18,400 tokens total)
- Request: request-2345 (18,400 tokens)
- Model per-tile cap: 20,000 (so no cap split) but billing quantum/minimum: 1,000 tokens per billed unit -> billed = ceil(18,400/1,000)*1,000 = 19,000 tokens
- Invoice lines: single line request-2345 (19,000 billed)

Edge cases to call out:
- Very small tails: e.g., a 50-token tail will still hit the 1,000-token minimum (if quantum/minimum applies), which can look like an "extra" spike on the invoice.
- Cross-day split: if processing spans UTC day boundary, tiles are time-stamped where they completed and will show on that day's invoice.
- KV-cache reuse: when tiles reuse cached KV across requests, we credit reuse at the invoice/commit level but the raw tile lines still appear (we apply KV reuse credits on a separate adjustment line).

Ill produce a short sample mapping (CSV-style) and attach. Vanessa/Neha — can you confirm the exact billing quantum for Acme under the current commitment (I have a guess of 1,000 tokens but want to be sure) and whether they are on a per-request minimum waiver?

Happy to hop on a 20 min call if Rajivs team wants us to walk through a live example.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 10 Sep 2025 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Context tiling / invoice example ask

Rajiv —

Confirmed: Acme is on the 1,000-token billing quantum under the current enterprise commitment, and there is no blanket per-request minimum waiver in the contract. That means tiles under 1,000 tokens round up to 1,000. We can provide one-off credits where appropriate (we did this for a pilot last quarter) but that requires a request from your finance lead.

Attached is a small CSV I generated from Marcus's examples (context-tiling-examples.csv) showing the mapping from raw token count to billed units and the invoice line name. For your GL team, the helpful columns are: original_request_id, tile_index, raw_tokens, billed_tokens, invoice_line_id, invoice_date.

If you want, we can produce the exact mapping for the August invoice extract you sent and propose any credits for tiles that look like systemic measurement artifacts.

Thanks —
